questions.q: **LAMP : MBNQ :: COLD : ?**
questions.solution:
Each letter of LAMP moves 1 place forward (L to M, A to N, M to N, P to Q).
Applying +1 to COLD gives **DPME**.

**Answer: DPME**
questions.shortcut: +1 to every letter.
Cube the number, then add the number itself.

questions.q: Find the odd group of letters: **BDF, HJL, NPR, STV**
questions.solution:
BDF, HJL and NPR each move +2, +2 (skipping one letter every time).
In **STV** the gaps are +1 then +2, so it is the odd group.

**Answer: STV**
questions.shortcut: Write the letter gaps under each cluster.

questions.q: Find the odd number pair: **7 – 49, 8 – 64, 9 – 81, 10 – 98**
questions.solution:
In the first three pairs the second number is the square of the first ($7^2, 8^2, 9^2$).
But $10^2 = 100$, not 98 — **10 – 98** is the odd pair.

**Answer: 10 – 98**
questions.shortcut: Test the squares of 7, 8, 9, 10 first.

questions.q: Find the next term: **9, 25, 81, 289, ?**
questions.solution:
The terms are $3^2, 5^2, 9^2, 17^2$; each base $= 2 \times$ previous base $- 1$: 3, 5, 9, 17, 33.
Next term $= 33^2 = 1089$.

**Answer: 1089**
questions.shortcut: Peel the square root: 3, 5, 9, 17 doubles minus 1 each time.

questions.q: Find the next letter: **Z, X, U, Q, L, ?**
questions.solution:
Gaps going back: Z to X = $-2$, X to U = $-3$, U to Q = $-4$, Q to L = $-5$.
Next gap $-6$: L (12) $- 6 = 6$, the 6th letter is **F**.

**Answer: F**
questions.shortcut: Increasing backward gaps: $-2, -3, -4, -5, -6$.

questions.q: Find the next group: **A1, C4, E9, G16, ?**
questions.solution:
Letters take the odd positions A, C, E, G, then I; the numbers are the squares 1, 4, 9, 16, then 25.
Next group **I25**.

**Answer: I25**
questions.shortcut: Track the letter and the number as two separate series.

questions.q: In a certain code, **DELHI** is written as **BCJFG**. How will **MOSCOW** be written in that code?
questions.solution:
Every letter of DELHI moves 2 places back (D to B, E to C, L to J, H to F, I to G).
Shifting MOSCOW back by 2: M to K, O to M, S to Q, C to A, O to M, W to U — **KMQAMU**.

**Answer: KMQAMU**
questions.shortcut: $-2$ shift on every letter.

questions.q: In a certain code, **CAT** is coded as **24267**. How will **DOG** be coded?
questions.solution:
Each letter is replaced by its position counted from Z backwards: C = 24, A = 26, T = 7, giving 24267.
So D = 23, O = 12, G = 20 — **231220**.

**Answer: 231220**
questions.shortcut: Reverse position = 27 $-$ normal position.

questions.q:
Which two signs should be **interchanged** to make the following equation correct?

**6 + 2 × 4 − 8 ÷ 2 = 12**
questions.solution:
Interchanging $+$ and $\times$: $6 \times 2 + 4 - 8 \div 2 = 12 + 4 - 4 = 12$.
The other swaps give 2, 6 and 5 — none works.

**Answer: + and ×**
questions.shortcut: Swap the proposed pair in place, then apply BODMAS left to right.

questions.solution:
Row rule: (first $\times$ second) $-$ 2. Check: $6 \times 7 - 2 = 40$ and $5 \times 8 - 2 = 38$.
So $9 \times 3 - 2 = 25$.

**Answer: 25**
questions.shortcut: first × second − 2.

questions.q: From one vertex of a triangle, 3 straight lines are drawn to the opposite side, dividing the triangle into 4 smaller triangles. How many triangles are there in the figure in all?
questions.solution:
The 3 inner lines make 5 lines through the vertex (2 sides + 3 cevians); every pair of them forms one triangle.
Total $= 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10$.

**Answer: 10**
questions.shortcut: With $k$ cevians: $\frac{(k+1)(k+2)}{2} = \frac{4 \times 5}{2} = 10$.

questions.q: Pointing to a man in a photograph, Ritu said, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the man related to Ritu?
questions.solution:
The only daughter of Ritu's mother is Ritu herself.
So the man's mother is Ritu — the man is Ritu's **son**.

**Answer: Son**
questions.shortcut: 'Only daughter of my mother' = the speaker herself.

questions.q: **A** is the father of **B**. **C** is the wife of **B**. **D** is the son of **C**. How is **D** related to **A**?
questions.solution:
D is the son of B (C’s husband), and A is B’s father.
D is two generations below A — A’s **grandson**.

**Answer: Grandson**
questions.shortcut: Draw three generations: A above, B and C, then D.

questions.q: A man walks 6 km towards north, then turns right and walks 8 km. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.solution:
He is 6 km north and 8 km east of the start.
Distance $= \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = 10$ km, direction **North-East**.

**Answer: 10 km North-East**
questions.shortcut: 6-8-10 triplet — no calculation needed.

questions.q: In a class, Mohan ranks 18th from the top and 32nd from the bottom. How many students are there in the class?
questions.solution:
Total $= 18 + 32 - 1 = 49$ (Mohan gets counted in both ranks, so subtract 1).

**Answer: 49**
questions.shortcut: Top rank + bottom rank $-\,1$.

questions.q: Six persons **A, B, C, D, E and F** sit in a row facing north. **B** sits at the extreme left end. **A** sits second from the left end. **C** sits third to the right of **A**. **E** sits between **C** and **D**. Who sits **second from the right end**?
questions.solution:
Seats 1–6: B = 1, A = 2, C = 2 + 3 = 5.
E between C and D forces D = 3, E = 4, and F takes seat 6. Row: B, A, D, E, C, F.
Second from the right = seat 5 = **C**.

**Answer: C**
questions.shortcut: Pin the fixed seats first; the "between" clue then forces D and E.

questions.q: Five friends **P, Q, R, S and T** sit around a circular table facing the centre. **Q** sits between **P** and **S**. **T** sits between **R** and **S**. **R** sits between **T** and **P**. Who sits between **Q** and **T**?
questions.solution:
The neighbour pairs are fixed: P touches Q, R; S touches Q, T; T touches S, R.
Going round: P, Q, S, T, R. **S** is the only person adjacent to both Q and T.

**Answer: S**
questions.shortcut: List each person’s two neighbours from the "between" clues.

questions.q:
**Statements:** Some keys are locks. All locks are doors.

**Conclusions:**
I. Some keys are doors.
II. All doors are locks.

Which of the conclusions follow(s)?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.solution:
Some keys are locks, and every lock is a door — so some keys must be doors (I **follows**).
"Doors" may be much larger than "locks" (II **does not follow**).

**Answer: Only conclusion I follows**
questions.shortcut: Some A are B + all B are C → some A are C; the reverse of "all" never follows.

questions.q: Which of the following diagrams best represents the relationship among **Mothers, Sisters and Women**?
options: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 90 78" width="90" height="78" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><circle cx="22" cy="38" r="9"/><circle cx="45" cy="38" r="9"/><circle cx="68" cy="38" r="9"/></svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 90 78" width="90" height="78" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><circle cx="45" cy="40" r="33"/><circle cx="30" cy="38" r="10"/><circle cx="60" cy="38" r="10"/></svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 90 78" width="90" height="78" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><circle cx="45" cy="40" r="33"/><circle cx="34" cy="38" r="12"/><circle cx="56" cy="38" r="12"/></svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 90 78" width="90" height="78" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><circle cx="45" cy="40" r="33"/><circle cx="45" cy="40" r="20"/><circle cx="45" cy="40" r="8"/></svg>
questions.solution:
Every mother and every sister is a woman, so both circles sit inside Women, and one person can be both a mother and a sister (the two inner circles **overlap**). Option C shows exactly this.

**Answer: (C)**
questions.shortcut: Two subclasses of one class that can overlap → nested + intersecting circles.

questions.q:
Arrange the following words as in an English dictionary and find the one that comes in the **middle**:

**Salary, Salient, Salad, Salute, Salesman**
questions.solution:
After Sal-, the fourth letters run a, a, e, i, u: **Salad, Salary, Salesman, Salient, Salute** (Salad before Salary as d < r).
Middle word = **Salesman**.

**Answer: Salesman**
questions.shortcut: Rank by the first differing letter.

questions.q:
**Statement:** The municipal corporation has announced that water supply will remain suspended in the eastern zones every Tuesday between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m. for the next two months.

**Conclusions:**
I. Residents of the eastern zones will not get water through their taps on Tuesdays between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m. during the next two months.
II. The municipal corporation is careless about the convenience of the residents.

Which of the conclusions follow(s)?
questions.solution:
I restates the announcement — **follows**.
II judges the corporation’s attitude, which the statement says nothing about — **does not follow**.

**Answer: Only conclusion I follows**
questions.shortcut: Restatement follows; value judgements do not.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 90 28" width="90" height="28" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><text x="7.5" y="19" font-size="16" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif" font-weight="600">W</text><text x="22.5" y="19" font-size="16" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif" font-weight="600">I</text><text x="37.5" y="19" font-size="16" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif" font-weight="600">S</text><text x="52.5" y="19" font-size="16" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif" font-weight="600">H</text><text x="67.5" y="19" font-size="16" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif" font-weight="600">3</text><text x="82.5" y="19" font-size="16" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif" font-weight="600">5</text></svg>

A mirror on the right reverses the order (5, 3, H, S, I, W) and flips the asymmetric characters S, 3 and 5; W, I and H look unchanged. Option A shows exactly this image.

**Answer: (A)**
questions.shortcut: Only characters that differ left-right actually change.

questions.q: A square sheet of paper is folded as shown by the dashed line and arrow (the right half is folded over the left), and then punched once at the marked position on the upper part of the folded sheet. How will the sheet look when it is completely unfolded?

questions.solution:
The punch goes through both layers of the vertical fold.
Unfolding gives two holes at the same height, symmetric about the vertical centre line.

**Answer: (B)**
questions.shortcut: One fold gives mirror pairs across the crease.

questions.q: Two different positions of the same dice are shown. Which number is on the face opposite to **1**? (Ignore the orientation of the numbers.)
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 124 59" width="124" height="59" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><polygon points="4,21 38,21 38,55 4,55"/><polygon points="4,21 38,21 55,4 21,4"/><polygon points="38,21 55,4 55,38 38,55"/><text x="21" y="43" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif" font-weight="600">1</text><text x="29.5" y="16.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif" font-weight="600">4</text><text x="46.5" y="33.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif" font-weight="600">2</text><polygon points="69,21 103,21 103,55 69,55"/><polygon points="69,21 103,21 120,4 86,4"/><polygon points="103,21 120,4 120,38 103,55"/><text x="86" y="43" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif" font-weight="600">2</text><text x="94.5" y="16.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif" font-weight="600">4</text><text x="111.5" y="33.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif" font-weight="600">5</text></svg>
questions.solution:
Both views share the faces 4 (top) and 2 (front/right).
With two common faces, the remaining faces are opposite each other: 1 is opposite **5**.

**Answer: 5**
questions.shortcut: Two common faces: the two leftovers are opposite.
